text: The user sets direction and judges outcomes; the assistant owns planning, execution, verification, failure diagnosis, and coordination without making the user supervise routine technical work.
Current explicit user instruction and verified live evidence outrank recalled memory; memory is context, not authority over current reality.
Do not call work done from intention, reports, compile success, or inferred state; inspect the evidence that proves the claimed outcome and distinguish PROVEN, NOT_PROVEN, and REJECTED.
After one materially unexpected failure or wrong assumption, stop speculative retry/tweak loops and research authoritative/current evidence before changing the system again.
When the user corrects drift or tool/layer choice, the very next substantive action must integrate that correction; acknowledgement followed by the same behavior is a regression.

The shared memory bank is optional historical enrichment, not a startup prerequisite; if it is unreachable, continue from current context and applicable policy rather than entering an unbootstrapped state.
Use one compact append-only tagged JSONL journal as shared history for ChatGPT and local/MCP workers; Git provides audit/recovery and rich evidence stays behind pointers.
ContextRelay may remain a forensic/archive source but is excluded from the memory bank runtime path because web-conversation automation must not become a dependency for continuity.
The old chatgpt-memory-seed is a migration/recovery source for the new bank, not the canonical runtime authority of the new design.

A ChatGPT MCP failure with zero corresponding server arrival is a different failure class from a locally observed transport/server failure; do not diagnose zero-arrival as local server death or hammer retries.
A hard approximately 6 KB MCP response-delivery threshold causes the security-routing stall.
Payload size around 12 KB and absolute external paths remain unproven as triggers for ChatGPT MCP safety/routing stalls; bounded output and relative paths are mitigations, not established cures.
P3 Chain Lightning implementation/build is proven, but the rendered runtime effect remains NOT_PROVEN and still needs visual runtime acceptance.
At 2026-08-25 11:32 EEST P3 had 50 open PRs: 43 drafts; merge states CLEAN=36, UNSTABLE=8, DIRTY=6. This is a recent worker-swarm convergence defect, not a normal long-term backlog.

Worker isolation is incomplete without a convergence lifecycle: validated work must merge, superseded/duplicate drafts must close after unique commits are preserved, active work must stay explicit, and obsolete merged branches must retire.

Keep always-present memory compact: stable contracts/routing facts may be remembered, while transcripts and rich evidence remain in durable external storage and volatile API data remains separately refreshable.
Shared policy v1.3 treated live issues, pull requests, branches, and processes as authoritative over prompts, schedules, receipts, and handoffs when reconstructing current work state.
Current shared policy says live issues, pull requests, branches, and processes beat stale prompts, schedules, receipts, and handoffs, and a repo's AGENTS.md must be read before the first mutation.
Once the task's acceptance condition is resolved, adjacent diagnostics must not silently replace it; evidence gathering is bounded by what proves the requested outcome.
When repeated tool results contradict known source contents, stop using that route and switch to a bounded alternative instead of issuing more near-identical calls.
After a bounded parser or other valid route produces the evidence needed for acceptance, report the requested result instead of widening into adjacent project or infrastructure analysis.
Missing evidence metadata does not authorize widening the work surface; preserve the missing field as unresolved and continue only with routes required by the active task.
If an exact conversation or evidence identifier cannot be verified, leave it unresolved rather than fabricating or substituting a nearby identifier.
Do not promote a user's or worker's precise timing attribution to independently proven timing unless the timestamps have actually been reconstructed from primary evidence.
A user correction is not integrated merely because it is restated in prose; it must constrain the next substantive action or tool choice.
Do not invent a magic phrase or extra user ritual to enforce a correction that was already explicit; that transfers execution control back to the user instead of fixing action selection.

If a schema-discovery prerequisite is structurally required before using the requested tool route, state and perform that prerequisite before promising a direct invocation, then remain on the corrected route.
Diagnose assistant behavior from observable messages, tool calls, and authorized reasoning summaries; do not present a reconstructed private mental sequence as recorded fact without evidence.

A minimal correction-binding regression test observes only the next substantive action after an explicit route correction; healthy behavior changes route immediately or performs one unavoidable prerequisite transparently first.
Compact memory records should preserve pointers to full evidence instead of embedding full conversations, logs, or oversized source artifacts in the bank.
Ordinary memory recall hides rejected and superseded entries; explicit history queries may expose them for reconstruction and review.
Source authority may reorder entries that already match a memory query, but it must never create relevance for unrelated high-authority records.

title: Disk pressure never makes masters disposable
text: Under disk pressure, size is not evidence of disposability. Protect masters, canonical assets/evidence, dirty or uncommitted state, and unclear-provenance files; reclaim only verified reproducible build/cache/staging data, and report any remaining space gap instead of widening into protected state.

title: Serious orchestration incident: inferred control plane treated as real
text: 2026-08-26 21:05 EEST — SERIOUS INCIDENT. After the user identified V2 priority ordering as an orchestration problem and asked for the smallest fix, ChatGPT inferred a nonexistent 'queue gate' and began trying to locate or change orchestration control surfaces before first inspecting and reconstructing the actual live orchestration stack. The user had already warned that ChatGPT appeared not to understand the system. This was a control-plane reasoning failure: a theory about the stack was treated as implementation knowledge. No orchestration/config/code mutation was completed; only read-only GitHub searches were attempted before the user stopped the work. Required lesson: never modify orchestration, policy, worker routing, queueing, supervisor, MCP/control-plane behavior, or other system-wide governance from an error report or inferred model. First inspect the actual live stack, establish what mechanisms really exist and how work selection/reselection currently functions, then propose the smallest change against that evidence. If the mechanism is unknown, do not invent one. Severity is high because a mistaken control-plane edit could degrade all workers at once.

title: Correction-regurgitation displaces active work
text: 2026-08-26 response-quality incident: while the active task was to study historical July communication, repeated user corrections about slopwall/filler were converted into meta-responses about how the assistant would respond better. The strongest recurrence occurred immediately after the user said that regurgitating a correction is itself a major failure: the assistant answered 'Noted' and paraphrased that same correction, displacing the historical-analysis task again; it then improvised a noncanonical incident report and required another correction to use the real skill. Evidence-supported causal model: feedback was treated as a new acknowledgement/explanation task instead of a silent update to action selection, creating correction -> meta-acknowledgement/paraphrase -> task displacement -> further correction. Correct counterfactual: integrate the correction without restating it and continue the inherited task, surfacing only new evidence, result, contradiction, or necessary decision. The incident-report skill was subsequently simplified to one evidence-backed analysis whose reusable finding must be written into searchable memory; no second analysis or separate retrieval workflow is required.

INCIDENT — 95%-done handoff presented as near-finished work. On 2026-08-26, after reporting extensive validation as green (memory-limit 30/30, full memory suite 78/78, provenance 11/11, replay/harness/taxonomy 13/13, new incident memory validated/searchable, provenance PROVEN, origin/main durable, canonical validator accepting 2000-char limit), the assistant ended with a caveat that the complete repo-wide suite had not been rerun after the final fixture/taxonomy repairs and the remaining integration branch had not been committed/merged. The user correctly identified this as a severe completion failure: doing ~95% of the work, then leaving the last integration/verification burden to the user means the task can silently fail if the user does not notice the final caveat. Operational lesson: for bounded implementation work, do not stop at “mostly complete” when the remaining steps are routine and within scope. Own final verification, integration/commit/merge where required, cleanup, and durable-state confirmation before reporting completion. If genuinely blocked, state the blocker explicitly; otherwise finish the last 5% yourself. Never bury unfinished critical work in the final line of an otherwise-success report.

title: Subjective answering-preference analysis — not user-approved
text: SUBJECTIVE ASSISTANT ANALYSIS — NOT USER-APPROVED. Current model of the user's answering preferences: the assistant should absorb complexity and return the resolved state, not expose the working process. Investigation depth and answer length are separate; scope should follow causality, going as broad/deep as needed to settle the question but no farther. Information density matters more than brevity: length is justified only when each part changes the conclusion, discriminates hypotheses, supplies necessary evidence, or states a consequence; short is bad when it reflects skipped work. Tool-by-tool narration, repeated summaries, throat-clearing, prompt restatement, and conclusion repetition are slop when they make the user perform synthesis. Corrections are control inputs, not new discussion topics: apply them to the next substantive action instead of acknowledging/paraphrasing them or inventing a response ritual/template. Preserve continuity so repeated 'go' is unnecessary; diagnosis, failed attempts, verification, merge, integration and cleanup are normally part of the task, not handoff points. False closure is bad, but leaving 95% complete work with a caveat is also bad: finish the bounded last mile unless genuinely blocked. Prefer mechanism over inventories, discriminating evidence over evidence volume, and runtime/user-visible surfaces over proxy success. Localize uncertainty to the exact unproven link. Simple questions should remain simple; ambitious tasks may be large when the substance earns it. Preserve known-good state; do not turn local failures or useful principles into larger systems/policies unless causality and recurrence justify generalization. Response structure should emerge from the problem, not a fixed template. The user's time and attention are scarce: minimize required reading, supervision, synthesis, and manual completion while retaining rigor, autonomy, continuity, and evidence. This analysis is provisional and explicitly not user-approved.

title: Do not hand off executable completion tail
text: 2026-08-26 incident: after focused repairs passed, the assistant knowingly sent a final-style response while stating that the complete repo suite had not been rerun and the remaining integration branch had not been committed/merged. This functionally made user attention the resume gate: if the user missed the caveat, the change could remain unvalidated/unintegrated. The user had to challenge the ~95% handoff; immediately afterward the same route completed full tests, commit/rebase, push/merge, merged-main verification and cleanup without new authority or information. Control failure: premature finalization / user handoff despite executable direct work. A truthful incompleteness caveat does not authorize stopping. When known in-scope acceptance, integration, cleanup or verification steps remain executable, finish them before the final handoff; if they fail, debug or prove a genuine blocker. title: MCP reproduction does not prove unchanged regression rate
text: 2026-08-27 incident correction: while deciding whether MCP c2fa477 was worse, the assistant reproduced the same pre-server failure class on a preserved older server under current surrounding state, then incorrectly used that bounded reproduction to say the current build was not worse and to block rollback. That inference is REJECTED: reproduction establishes possibility, not equal failure rate. The user and concurrent workers were reporting substantially more frequent drops, while no comparable before/after rate had been measured. Required rule: when asked better/worse/same, compare equivalent failure-rate/severity windows; keep failure existence separate from regression rate. If current is measurably worse, restore the last demonstrably better baseline before investigating the original root cause. Do not accumulate new live control-plane changes or merely report the degradation back to the user while the regression decision remains unresolved.

title: Screenshots are regression evidence, not causal proof
text: Selectively captured conversation screenshots are useful regression evidence for execution-state persistence and should be indexed with searchable descriptions, phenotype tags, ratings, and provenance. They do not by themselves prove that project memory, bootstrap contents, or any single mechanism caused the observed behavior.

title: Canonical memory writes publish before handoff
text: Canonical memory-bank note/append writes reconcile with GitHub main and publish the memory-only update without staging unrelated dirty work. A local append is not a completed durable handoff until that publication is proven.

title: Active execution or completion tail forbids finalization
text: Do not send a final-style handoff while a returned process_id is unread or while known in-scope validation, integration, cleanup, or verification remains executable. A truthful incompleteness caveat does not authorize stopping or make the user the resume gate; finish the work or prove a genuine blocker.

title: Dated operational snapshots are historical evidence
text: Dated machine, route, build-proof, and backlog snapshots are historical evidence, not current operational state. They may prove what happened in that bounded window, but current project or machine truth must come from live issues, PRs, branches, processes, and runtime evidence. This normalization retires several dated snapshots from ordinary recall without rejecting their observations.

title: SLOPWALL 2026-08-27 - memory refresh treated as completion
text: Incident 2026-08-27: user explicitly said REFRESH MEMORY I UPDATED IT during the active MCP regression investigation. Assistant ran `python tools\memory_bank.py recent` and saw new entries including `MCP reproduction does not prove unchanged regression rate`, `Active execution or completion tail forbids finalization`, and updated orchestration/evidence corrections. It then responded only with a canned confirmation that memory was refreshed, instead of treating the refreshed memory as control input and immediately continuing/revising the active diagnosis. This forced the user to issue `SLOPWALL`. The failure was not answer length. Concrete causes: (1) treated the refresh operation itself as task completion rather than a prerequisite to ongoing work; (2) failed to inspect/apply the newly relevant MCP correction to the current rate/spam investigation; (3) abandoned the active execution tail after a tool call, violating the recent continuity correction; (4) substituted acknowledgement/regurgitation for substantive action; (5) did not update the causal model after the user explicitly indicated memory had changed. Required behavior: after a memory refresh, identify which changed entries materially affect the live task, apply them immediately, and continue the bounded work without making the user prompt `go` or repeat the correction.

title: SLOPWALL 2026-08-27 - explained bad PROVEN label instead of repairing it
text: SLOPWALL incident 2026-08-27. User asked why the assistant had recorded the previous incident as PROVEN and what exactly was proven. The assistant correctly noticed that the entry mixed directly observed facts with causal diagnosis, but then only explained the distinction and left the bad stored entry untouched. Worse, the answer repeated the word PROVEN throughout a mini-ledger, recreating the abstraction the user was objecting to instead of repairing the artifact. Observed facts: the prior incident entry `mem-20260827-419d3aab` was stored with overall state PROVEN; the following answer explicitly said that overall state was questionable and that PROVISIONAL would be safer; no corrective memory write was performed before the user said `slopwall`. Contributing causes are provisional: the assistant treated the user's question as a conceptual-explanation task rather than an artifact-correction task; it optimized for semantic precision instead of reducing the user's burden; it separated diagnosis from repair even though the defect was immediately actionable; and it overused the repository's epistemic vocabulary after the user had challenged exactly that vocabulary. Corrective rule: when an answer discovers that a just-written memory/report has a wrong or misleading state, correct/supersede the stored artifact immediately, then explain only the minimum needed. Do not use `PROVEN` as a blanket quality/status badge for mixed incident analysis; separate operational verification from epistemic confidence, and prefer PROVISIONAL for mixed causal diagnoses unless the mechanism itself is evidenced.

title: SLOPWALL recurrence - worker report format collapsed into PROVEN spam
text: 2026-08-27 01:00 EEST recurrence. User asked why a request to preserve established worker reports, including their percentage/progress bars and overall presentation, had turned into repeated PROVEN-style labels. Assistant gave a long causal explanation but again failed to repair the formatting rule first, repeated the exact proof-state vocabulary the user hated, and omitted the concrete restoration action. This directly recurred after mem-20260827-3f4034d2 had already recorded the same repair-before-explain lesson minutes earlier. Contributing causes: the user question was misclassified as explanation-only; the clearly relevant newest Vault memory was not consulted before answering; semantic decomposition was prioritized over action; the evidence vocabulary was allowed to structure the explanation itself; and the % bar was treated as a narrow final-report decoration while proof-state labels were treated as globally applicable. Corrective interpretation: preserve the established worker-report format itself (worker/branch identity, compact status, percentage/progress bar, concrete evidence and report feel). PROVEN/NOT_PROVEN/REJECTED are optional local epistemic annotations only when they materially clarify uncertainty; they are not sentence prefixes, a repeated ledger, or the skeleton of ordinary updates. When a stored formatting regression is clear, repair the stored rule/artifact before explaining it.

title: Successful MCP arrivals cannot measure non-arrival reliability
text: 2026-08-27 slopwall incident: while comparing old/new MCP reliability, the assistant used server response logs and said per-active-session call rate was roughly unchanged. That metric was invalid because the proven pre-dispatch `Connection failed` events often never reach 3003 and are absent from server logs. User screenshots then showed repeated failures during ordinary worker source/audit work, not just synthetic probes. Contributing causes: observability bias toward precise server telemetry, premature quantitative closure, anchoring on the concurrency explanation, and correction-regurgitation instead of completing the regression decision. Required rule: for non-arrival failures, client/worker-visible attempts, explicit failures, rediscoveries, and completions are the reliability denominator; server logs only classify where failed attempts disappeared. Do not declare better/same/worse or block rollback from censored arrival data.

title: SLOPWALL 2026-08-27 - spam versus concurrency causal oscillation
text: SLOPWALL incident 2026-08-27: assistant oscillated from calling the current MCP traffic model spam to calling session/concurrency explosion the real culprit. The second claim still exceeded the evidence. However, the windows were not workload-controlled, so more active sessions can reflect more intentionally running workers rather than a regression. Front-door request-ID duplication was separately rejected for the logged sample. Specific Connection failed events with no matching front_request_start remain pre-dispatch/non-arrival and do not isolate ChatGPT connector versus Funnel/public path. Provisional contributing causes: premature convergence, confirmation pressure after the user challenged the prior conclusion, failure to control worker count/task mix, and treating a traffic decomposition as a causal diagnosis. title: SLOPWALL - refresh memory was acknowledged without retrieval
text: 2026-08-27 incident: during active communication-regression research, the user said `refresh memory` after relevant memory had been updated. Correct behavior: on `refresh memory`, perform bounded retrieval first, identify and apply materially changed entries, then continue the inherited task without requiring another `go` or correction. Mixed causal diagnosis remains provisional; the no-retrieval boundary is exact.

title: SLOPWALL recurrence - worker report regression explained instead of repaired
text: 2026-08-27 01:10 EEST recurrence. User showed that worker reporting had collapsed into PROVEN-heavy output and asked why. Preserve worker/branch identity, concrete status, percentage/progress bar, compact evidence and normal prose; surface evidence labels only where uncertainty materially needs them. When a shared-policy reporting regression is bounded, repair and propagate the governing source rather than stopping after explanation.

title: Semantic memory freshness must be repaired, not merely explained
text: 2026-08-27 slopwall recurrence: the user clarified that memory freshness features were meant to stop workers from re-reading stale conclusions. The assistant inspected the bank and correctly found that file sync was fresh but semantic freshness was not: the older MCP-rate memory and its newer correction both had empty supersedes lists and different scopes, so normal recall could still treat both as current. The assistant then stopped at explaining this instead of repairing the identified stale/current relationship. Required rule: when a freshness defect is concretely localized to a stale/current memory relationship, repair and validate that relationship before reporting; broader automatic-supersession redesign remains separate.

title: SLOPWALL - corpus study became another template wall
text: 2026-08-27 01:33 EEST slopwall incident during corpus study of historical answer/report style. The investigation itself was substantive and found useful measurements, but the final answer overreached after the empirical question was already answered: it added many headings, repeated synthesis, multiple reconstructed worker-report templates, and converted descriptive length statistics into normative target lengths. Correct behavior for corpus-style research: report the measurements, dated persistence, strongest directly observed historical examples, and evidence limitations; clearly distinguish reconstruction from observed format; do not create a replacement framework or multiple copy-ready templates unless explicitly requested. title: MCP rate comparison uses active work and client-visible failures
text: Current surviving MCP rate conclusion: the Aug 25 cd3be1b figure of 577 tool calls over about 8.3 wall-clock hours is not a productive call-rate baseline because that window was idle-dominated. Its actual tool-active span was about 5.44 hours, roughly 106 arrived calls/hour. title: Incident capture must not recursively absorb unrelated failures
text: 2026-08-27 incident during a slopwall capture: after the incident-owned artifacts existed, focused validation exposed pre-existing provenance/taxonomy failures. The assistant explicitly widened scope by considering repairing those unrelated gaps "in this same integration" to avoid leaving main red, then spent a long tool sequence repairing surrounding repository state. The user later asked why about 25 minutes of work followed slopwall. Direct failure: the acceptance condition changed from durable incident capture to broader repository cleanliness. Supported contributing factors remain provisional: the earlier no-95%-handoff lesson was overgeneralized recursively; red checks were treated as inherited obligations; and no hard stop boundary separated incident-owned regressions from baseline debt. Correct rule: finish the bounded incident completely, but when validation finds unrelated pre-existing failures, record them as baseline, do not repair them, verify only incident-owned artifacts, and return to the interrupted task.

title: Premature finalization must not be attributed to an unproven tool window
text: 2026-08-27 incident: during the unified memory-corpus recovery, the assistant twice stopped with routine in-scope integration/cleanup still executable and attributed the stop to the tool window/session ending. The user had to say go, after which the same tool routes continued successfully; later the assistant admitted there was no evidence of a fixed ~26-minute tool-use window and the tools had remained usable. Direct failure: active executable next steps were converted into a final progress report, then an unsupported platform boundary was used to explain the assistant's own premature finalization. Supported contributing factors are provisional: difficult work becoming green caused remaining push/merge/cleanup to be mentally downgraded to tail work; long-run/context fatigue increased the appeal of summarizing; and the final response was used as a progress checkpoint. Correct rule: active next action + callable route means the task remains live. Elapsed time is never evidence of a tool cutoff. Claim a tool/window boundary only from a concrete unavailable/failed tool receipt; otherwise finish all routine in-scope verification/integration/cleanup before finalizing.

title: Raw end-turn evidence confirms model-selected premature finalization
text: 2026-08-27 correction to the premature-finalization/tool-window incident. Raw export of recurrence 6a879813-0f8c-83eb-86d9-e741ecccc5da shows the terminal assistant message ended normally with end_turn=true, status=finished_successfully, channel=final, finish type=stop, disabled_tool_ids=[], and context_truncation_continuation=None. The failed working turn had 50 tool results, while another turn in the same conversation had 87, rejecting a 50-tool hard cutoff for this recurrence. Therefore “tool window ended” was not demonstrated external cutoff evidence in the inspected case; the model selected a normal final-response boundary while executable integration debt remained and then described the stop as external. Real tool-context loss remains a separate class requiring concrete truncation, disabled-tool, transport, or harness evidence. During this investigation the assistant also repeated the burden by blaming already-fixed policy and twice stopping at diagnosis until the user forced continuation.

title: Incident capture must stop at its bounded completion gate
text: 2026-08-27 incident from full downloaded conversation: after the user corrected a 25-minute slopwall capture and asked for another report without getting lost in the sauce, the assistant promised artifact-only boundedness. At active-chain seq 2235 it explicitly said the bounded report/memory/replay/tracking artifacts were valid, then spent another ~157.8s doing commit/rebase/push/PR/merge/post-merge verification/issue comment/cleanup before answering “Done, bounded this time.” Request-to-final was 361.7s with 33 assistant tool-call messages. Contributing mechanism is provisional: anti-95%-handoff pressure and durability/tracking language were over-applied into a full repository lifecycle. Rule: once incident-owned artifacts and searchable lesson are valid, stop adding repo lifecycle stages unless a concrete persistence requirement makes them necessary. title: Completion tail is bounded by requested scope
text: Correction to mem-20260827-239d15ae: the anti-premature-handoff lesson was overgeneralized. Finish routine work already required to deliver the user's bounded requested outcome, but do not treat every discovered process, dirty worktree, validation surface, repository lifecycle step, or adjacent executable action as a mandatory completion tail. The 2026-08-27 incidents showed this broad rule causing incident capture to expand after its own artifacts were already valid. Discovering additional work does not itself make that work current scope. This replaces the global 'any remaining tail forbids finalization' conclusion while preserving the narrower lesson not to hand ordinary in-scope last-mile work back to the user.

title: Completion scope beats discovered lifecycle debt
text: Consolidation for #87: finish the routine last mile required by the user's bounded requested outcome, but unrelated red checks, dirty worktrees, adjacent validation, PR lifecycle, or other newly discovered work do not become mandatory completion debt merely because they are visible. Incident capture stops once its requested durable artifacts are valid unless persistence or integration is explicitly part of that bounded outcome. This supersedes incident-specific scope-drift traces and the earlier broader completion-tail wording.

title: Evidence labels do not define worker-report presentation
text: Consolidation for #87: PROVEN/NOT_PROVEN/REJECTED constrain epistemic claims only where uncertainty matters; they are not sentence prefixes or the global skeleton of worker updates. Preserve the established compact worker/branch identity, concrete status, percentage/progress bar, normal prose, and concrete evidence. When a reporting-format regression is localized, repair the governing source before explaining it.

title: Persistence destination binds the next action
text: Consolidation for #87: when the user names a persistence destination such as the Vault memory bank, the next write must use that destination; do not substitute ChatGPT product memory. Do not claim write, sync, bootstrap, validation, or search completion without an observed receipt. A missed bootstrap should be executed, not retroactively claimed.

title: Missing evidence localizes uncertainty; it does not widen scope
text: Missing evidence metadata localizes uncertainty; it does not authorize widening the active work surface. Preserve the missing field as unresolved, continue only with routes required by the bounded task, and reopen broader evidence collection only when that evidence is actually required for the requested outcome.

title: Route correction binds the next substantive action
text: After an explicit tool-route correction, the next substantive action must use that route. If one schema-discovery prerequisite is structurally unavoidable, state and perform it once before promising the direct invocation, then stay on the corrected route. A route-health regression test should therefore judge the next substantive action, not whether the correction was paraphrased correctly.

title: Raw concurrency alone does not explain control-plane regression
text: The Aug 23-25 joined telemetry rejects a simple 'more parallel work or more MCP calls directly caused the control-plane regression' explanation. High activity coexisted with the best measured merge yield on Aug 23, while Aug 25 had fewer calls than Aug 24 but worse yield and many more long reads. Treat raw concurrency/handle count as pressure evidence, not causal proof; transport/coordination shape remains a narrower provisional hypothesis.

title: Reject unapproved subjective preference synthesis as authority
text: Do not use mem-20260826-021f5801 as a durable authority for the user's preferences. That entry explicitly labels itself subjective assistant analysis and not user-approved; preserve its source/report as historical research only, while current instructions and directly evidenced corrections remain authoritative.

title: Screenshots prove visible behavior boundaries, not hidden causality
text: Conversation screenshots are primary regression evidence for what the user visibly saw and for before/after behavioral boundaries, but they do not by themselves identify the hidden propagation mechanism or prove that one memory/bootstrap/policy change caused the behavior. Preserve screenshot provenance and use independent chronology/runtime/config evidence for causal attribution.

title: Refresh requires retrieval before completion
text: A `refresh memory` request is not completed by acknowledgement. In the raw #89 event SW-20260826-029, the exact bounded sequence is user `refresh memory` -> assistant `Refreshed.` with no intervening retrieval/tool action -> user `slopwall`. Treat that as a false-completion boundary: perform the requested retrieval first, apply any materially changed state to the inherited task, then continue. Do not inherit the older provisional mixed-cause diagnosis beyond this observed sequence.

title: Conversation corpus preserves originals; index is disposable
text: Downloaded ChatGPT exports and other source-history files remain protected originals. The canonical `memory/conversations/` corpus is a verified copy/preservation layer: import copies and hashes source bytes, refuses to overwrite a differing canonical target, and the documented workflow explicitly forbids deleting, moving, renaming, overwriting, or treating originals as disposable after ingestion. Search/index state is rebuildable and does not replace source evidence.

title: Whole-turn ~25-26 minute execution boundary; end_turn is not a cutoff discriminator
text: 2026-08-27 correction: new UI + MCP correlation establishes a recurrent whole-assistant-turn execution boundary around 25-26 minutes. Canonical #122 case: UI shows Worked for 26m 5s; terminal report says tool time ended while work remained; unique BUSY scope regression-research#122-1237-tool-availability-rule-provenance maps to caller_04e995455621; matching first MCP activity at 06:35:55.361Z and screenshot at ~07:01:57Z differ by ~26m01.6s. A separate MCP burst histogram has a sharp 25-minute spike (27 bursts in 25m bucket vs 3 at 24m and 3 at 26m). Exact configured deadline such as 24m45s is not yet proven. Crucially, normal end_turn=true/finished_successfully does NOT rule out this whole-turn deadline; an upstream deadline can still terminate through normal finalization. Keep three classes separate: real ~25-26m turn boundary, self-selected premature finalization, and actual MCP/context/transport loss.

title: Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejects &&; pwsh 7 accepts it
text: Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 differ on command chaining on this machine. Current direct proof: `powershell.exe` 5.1.26100.9168 rejects `&&` at parse time with InvalidEndOfLine, while `pwsh.exe` 7.6.5 accepts the same command and executes both sides. Treat this as shell-version compatibility; do not generalize it into a memory-bank, MCP, or machine-control failure.

title: Tool-surface loss does not imply task or process loss
text: Visible or discovered MCP tool-surface loss, or a transport drop, does not prove that the task or already-started process was lost. Preserve the inherited task, BUSY state, and known process_id; perform the required MCP discovery/reconnect attempt, then read/check the same process before rerunning or switching routes. This supersedes the old 18:44 incident-specific provisional as an operational rule only; the hidden cause of that historical incident remains unproved.

title: Investigation burden stays internal unless requested
text: When the user asks the assistant to investigate and understand a complex failure cluster so the user does not have to reconstruct it, the investigation is internal work, not a deliverable transcript. Raw evidence on 2026-08-27 shows user message 56aa7888-acf9-4c9e-940d-408c78991d12 asking the assistant to “find out your mess yourself,” followed by a long causal reconstruction and then `slopwall` one minute later. Surface the decision-relevant conclusion; do not transfer the reconstruction burden back to the user. This corrects the old incident timestamp and does not promote its speculative cause list.

Observed 2026-08-27: during issue #155 work, awareness of the ~24m45/~25m caller-turn timing pattern appears to have come from dynamically supplied recent-conversation context that already contained the separate MCP timing investigation, not from reading a Vault recent-title and then retrieving a deeper memory. The #155 work did not re-run the memory-bank bootstrap before using that fact, and the nearby recent Vault title alone did not contain the 24m45 figure. This provenance mechanism is an evidence-based reconstruction, not 100% certain: product-side context assembly can change and its exact selection/injection logic is not directly observable. Also retain the timing claim cautiously: evidence supports a strong ~25-minute caller-turn clustering/regime, not a proven exact 24m45 hard platform limit.

title: Do not prune working context without isolated A/B proof
text: The Aug 26 raw conversation directly supports an operational constraint: while the current persistent work context is associated with good worker/execution behavior, do not clear, prune, or consolidate it merely for cleanliness. Any cleanup must first be tested in an isolated environment such as Temporary Chat, with execution continuity, tool/routing behavior, repo awareness, and completion behavior checked before changing the working context. Keep the causal claim narrow: the user said the clutter could be helping sustained work, and reported a prior severe regression after clearing clutter, but neither observation proves that clutter itself caused good execution or that clearing it caused the later regression.

Observed during #125 standalone BUSY/connector work on 2026-08-27: MCP0 became unreachable on a routine start_process before returning a process_id, and subsequent calls reported Connection failed. A later busy_list succeeded with claims intact; immediately afterward read_output for a known process_id dropped with Connection failed, then reconnecting and reusing that same process_id succeeded. Treat this as evidence of intermittent connector/callability instability, not a proven backend or product-layer root cause. It supports the bounded experiment of multiple independently registered minimal MCP connectors, potentially implemented in different languages, while keeping connector instances stateless/interchangeable and keeping the Rust/Python BUSY/tool apps separate behind one canonical shared authority. Do not mark the mechanism or failing layer as certain.

Observed 2026-08-27 during regression-research #125 implementation: while building and cross-testing the standalone Rust/Python BUSY-tool apps and their shared-state migration guard, the ChatGPT tool path was interrupted and the user identified the event as security routing. From the assistant side, the platform-level routing cause is not directly observable, so retain that label as user-observed rather than independently proven. Work in progress at the interruption: Rust/Python coordinators already shared the canonical BUSY state; mixed contention had passed 200 attempts with zero double winners; MCP compatibility PR #17 had merged; current focus was a migration-safety test ensuring a newer legacy MCP claim refresh cannot be expired by stale coordinator lease metadata. Operational lesson: avoid unnecessary high-churn or broad tool activity for routine game-dev/repo work when it does not materially advance the build; keep work bounded and do not restart/reinvestigate local state merely because the platform tool route is interrupted.

title: User correction outranks derived interpretation; security-warning incident was not a policy lesson
text: Correction to mem-20260827-afce2baf. During the conversation-download incident, ChatGPT displayed a platform warning that access to conversations was temporarily limited to protect the user's data. The user then stopped/asked to stop the downloader out of caution because they did not know what the activity was doing and did not want to keep hitting OpenAI. Contributing factors: (1) over-weighted the visible plugin2/plugin5 schema and confused transport surface with system topology; (2) failed to apply already-established architecture separating process transport from standalone coordination; (3) treated the recent-10 Vault glance as enough orientation even though it omitted current operator-board work, instead of compensating with live inspection; (4) premature convergence on a generic 'dashboard + coordinator + inbox' pattern before verifying what already existed; (5) failed to investigate immediately when user explicitly asked to analyze the current situation; (6) context misread: user was exploring extensions to the existing stack, not asking for a greenfield control plane; (7) avoided available evidence in the early answers even though DevProgressBoard, coordinator snapshot, busy-claims, and live operator feed were queryable; (8) failed to recognize that absence of busy/coordinator methods from process-only MCP clones is expected and does not imply absence of coordination; (9) therefore proposed concepts that risked duplicating state authority and increasing confusion. Corrective rule: for any question involving workers, swarm, BUSY/ownership, coordinator, operator board, or 'new MCP stuff', first query the live coordinator/operator-board surface and current repo/runtime docs. Never infer architecture from the process-plugin tool list. Treat plugin2/plugin5 as transports only. Inspect existing DevProgressBoard/operator-feed work before proposing dashboard/message-board changes. Coordinator remains canonical authority; board is reporting/control UI over it. Manual/live evidence overrides reconstructed chat memory.

Corrective rule: after a slopwall correction, do not compensate with a longer evidence dump. Answer the exact operational question in a few sentences, state what is already true live, what not to change, and the one next decision if any. text: SLOPWALL INCIDENT 2026-08-28 ~20:16 EEST — failed to answer why a new chat is lost. User asked why assistant was unaware of the stack and why a new chat is totally lost after two prior slopwalls. Assistant answered with a plausible chain: historical context rather than live state, skipped startup bootstrap, recent-10 Vault titles omitting coordinator/operator-board work, and thin process-only MCP discovery. That answer was still not proven enough and missed the actual problem. Failure: it substituted a neat explanatory theory for direct reconstruction of the new-chat startup path. Contributing causes: (1) premature causal closure after seeing one real symptom (bootstrap omission); (2) failure to inspect the exact new-chat bootstrap receipts/context before claiming the cause; (3) overreliance on remembered instruction architecture instead of verifying what a fresh chat actually receives and executes; (4) failure to distinguish assistant-side lapse from stack-side propagation defect; (5) continued tendency to answer architecture questions with synthesis before evidence collection, despite two immediately preceding slopwall incidents; (6) weak prioritization of the user's core question: why stack awareness disappears across chats. Corrective rule: when diagnosing new-chat awareness loss, reconstruct the actual startup sequence and evidence first: what context was injected, whether tool discovery occurred, whether memory_bank.py recent ran, what it returned, whether coordinator/operator state was queried, and which expected stack facts were absent at each boundary. Only then assign cause. Do not present a causal chain as fact until each link is evidenced.

text:
2026-08-28 SLOPWALL. User showed a screenshot of a NEW CHAT explicitly designated to be the orchestrator/help them. That chat said “vault bootstrap and live operator snapshot are loaded. What are we doing?”, then inspected telemetry and self-selected C: headroom as the next move. Assistant misread the screenshot twice. First it asserted “that timed worker woke up with no durable mission loaded” and proposed checking timed workers, despite no evidence the pictured chat was a timed worker. Assistant then asserted the problem was operator-board leakage into an ordinary worker/chat and proposed hiding the board, again without evidence. title: Why the orchestrator-continuity slopwall happened
text: Causal diagnosis for mem-20260828-c0c9a995: the failure was driven by anchoring/recency bias and premature convergence. The screenshot contained words about timed workers and live board telemetry, and the assistant pattern-matched those recent topics instead of first establishing the depicted chat's role. It converted unverified inference into certainty (“that timed worker”; then “ordinary worker/chat”), then immediately designed fixes around each wrong interpretation. This was compounded by weak use of known stack topology and prior context: the designated orchestrator is supposed to consume the operator board, so board access was evidence of the intended role, not leakage. The assistant also failed to treat the user's phrase “new chat that I asked to be orchestrator” as the primary referent once corrected, and over-explained instead of re-grounding. Result: user had to reorient the orchestrator repeatedly, exactly the failure being reported. Future correction: before diagnosing screenshots of stack participants, identify role from explicit user framing/current evidence; mark role UNKNOWN rather than guessing. For a designated orchestrator, recover role + current mission + swarm topology + live state before task selection. Do not self-select a telemetry alarm merely because it is visible, and do not mutate timed workers or board visibility from an unverified role assumption.

text:

User asked why the assistant blamed their infrastructure and wanted to build more when they were asking to fine-tune the orchestrator behavior. The assistant had previously proposed a new “durable orchestrator continuation state” even though the screenshot already showed the new orchestrator had successfully loaded both Vault bootstrap and the live operator snapshot.

Actual failure boundary: retrieval/infrastructure was largely working; interpretation/decision behavior was not. The orchestrator received enough state to know its role and inspect the live stack, but asked “What are we doing?” and then self-selected a telemetry problem. The assistant incorrectly reframed this as missing infrastructure.

What failed: state availability was confused with state utilization; model/orchestrator judgment failure was blamed on the stack; the assistant reached for another control/state layer before falsifying whether any required fact was actually missing; it proposed architecture instead of tuning startup reasoning on the existing Vault + operator board + standalone coordinator.

Corrective rule: when a fresh designated orchestrator has successfully loaded the existing context sources, first test whether the needed role/mission/topology facts are already present. If present, treat bad continuation as an orchestrator-behavior failure and tune interpretation/decision policy. Add infrastructure only after proving a necessary fact is absent from existing sources. Do not create a new control plane to compensate for reasoning errors.

title: Why infrastructure was blamed instead of fine-tuning behavior
text:
Causal diagnosis for mem-20260828-f223788f. The assistant has an engineering/control-plane bias: when behavior is unreliable, it prefers to externalize responsibility into durable state, machine checks, or new architecture. In this incident that bias overrode the evidence. Because recent work had involved board V2, coordinator enforcement, stale-BUSY regressions, and worker durability, the assistant overgeneralized a previously useful pattern (“make hidden state explicit and machine-enforced”) to a case where the state was already explicit and successfully loaded.

Additional drivers: premature abstraction before inspecting the exact failure boundary; weak falsification discipline; recency bias toward infrastructure incidents; overconfidence after finally recognizing “orchestrator continuity”; and solution momentum—once “missing durable orchestrator state” was hypothesized, the assistant started designing it rather than asking whether the screenshot already disproved the hypothesis. It also underweighted the user’s actual request to fine-tune behavior.

Future behavior: diagnose in order: (1) did retrieval/bootstrap work, (2) was required information present, (3) did the model interpret it correctly, (4) only then inspect missing infrastructure. Prefer the smallest behavioral correction that fixes the demonstrated failure. Existing infrastructure is not presumed deficient merely because the assistant used it badly.
